skill.name: nodejs-backend-patterns
skill.description: Guidance for designing scalable, maintainable Node.js backends with TypeScript, API frameworks, layered architecture, security controls, databases, caching, and operational practices.
skill.summary: Apply practical architecture, security, data, and operations patterns to production Node.js backend projects.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are false positives caused by Markdown, TypeScript imports, template literals, environment configuration, and database examples. The all-interface network bind is a contextual exposure, and the playbook also contains unsafe SQL identifier interpolation, permissive CORS, and blocking Redis invalidation guidance.

remediation.issue: Update fields are interpolated into SQL without a runtime allowlist.
remediation.suggestion: Map accepted update properties to fixed column names, reject unknown keys, and keep all values parameterized.

remediation.issue: The Fastify example enables CORS for every reflected origin.
remediation.suggestion: Use an explicit production origin allowlist and document separate development settings.

remediation.issue: The Redis invalidation example uses KEYS and unrestricted patterns.
remediation.suggestion: Use cursor-based SCAN, namespace every cache key, restrict patterns, and delete matches in bounded batches.

remediation.issue: The Fastify server binds to every network interface.
remediation.suggestion: Explain when 0.0.0.0 is required and require firewall, proxy, or container network controls for production.

semantic_findings.title: Unvalidated SQL Identifier Interpolation
semantic_findings.description: The update example builds SQL column assignments from Object.keys(updates). Parameterized values do not protect interpolated identifiers, so unexpected request keys can alter the query.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The field names are directly interpolated into SQL while only values use placeholders. The example shows no runtime allowlist for accepted update keys.

semantic_findings.title: Permissive Fastify CORS Configuration
semantic_findings.description: The Fastify example reflects any request origin through origin: true. Production use can grant untrusted websites cross-origin access unless routes are strictly public.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The configuration explicitly enables dynamic origin reflection. The same playbook later warns against unrestricted production CORS, confirming this example needs qualification.

semantic_findings.title: Blocking Redis Pattern Invalidation
semantic_findings.description: The cache example uses Redis KEYS with an arbitrary pattern, then deletes every match. Large keyspaces or broad patterns can block Redis and remove unrelated cache entries.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The method accepts any pattern and directly calls KEYS followed by bulk deletion. Redis KEYS is synchronously expensive across large keyspaces.

content.value_statement: Backend projects often lack consistent architecture, security, and operational patterns. This skill provides TypeScript examples for APIs, data access, authentication, caching, and error handling.
actual_capabilities: Structures Express and Fastify applications with TypeScript.
Applies controller, service, repository, and dependency injection patterns.
Designs middleware for authentication, validation, rate limiting, logging, and errors.
Shows PostgreSQL, MongoDB, Redis, transaction, and connection pooling patterns.
Implements JWT authentication, role checks, password hashing, and token refresh flows.
Provides production checklists for security, monitoring, testing, and graceful shutdown.
limitations: The examples are reference patterns, not a complete runnable application.
Package versions and framework APIs require verification before implementation.
Deployment, cloud infrastructure, and environment-specific controls are not fully covered.
Testing guidance is brief and refers users to a separate testing skill.

use_cases.title: Design a New API
use_cases.description: Create a maintainable Express or Fastify service structure with clear HTTP, business, and data boundaries.
use_cases.target_user: Backend developer starting a Node.js service

use_cases.title: Standardize a Growing Service
use_cases.description: Refactor middleware, errors, dependencies, and repositories into consistent patterns that support team development.
use_cases.target_user: Technical lead improving an existing backend

use_cases.title: Review Production Readiness
use_cases.description: Assess authentication, validation, rate limits, logging, database pooling, caching, and shutdown behavior before release.
use_cases.target_user: Platform engineer reviewing a Node.js deployment

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Backend Framework
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare Express and Fastify for my API. Consider team experience, performance, validation, plugins, deployment, and maintenance. Recommend one with clear reasons.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Layered API Design
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a TypeScript Node.js API for [domain]. Define routes, controllers, services, repositories, validation, errors, dependencies, and a practical folder structure.

prompt_templates.title: Add Secure Authentication
prompt_templates.prompt: Design authentication and authorization for [application]. Include password hashing, access tokens, refresh rotation, role checks, secret validation, rate limits, and failure responses.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Backend Production Readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Node.js backend architecture for production. Identify security, reliability, scaling, data integrity, observability, caching, and shutdown risks. Prioritize concrete fixes.

output_examples.input: Design the architecture for a user management API using Express and PostgreSQL.
output: A layered structure separating routes, controllers, services, and repositories.
Validation and authentication middleware placed before controller handlers.
Parameterized repository operations with transactions for multi-step changes.
Central error handling, structured logs, health checks, and graceful shutdown.

output_examples.input: Review my JWT login and refresh flow for production risks.
output: A prioritized review covering secret validation, token lifetime, rotation, revocation, and replay protection.
Recommendations for generic credential errors, authentication rate limits, secure storage, and audit logging.
A verification checklist for expired, revoked, reused, and malformed tokens.

output_examples.input: Improve Redis cache invalidation for a large Node.js service.
output_examples.output: A bounded invalidation approach using namespaces, cursor scanning, batch deletion, metrics, and clear ownership of cache keys.

best_practices: Provide framework, database, deployment, and traffic constraints before requesting an architecture.
Validate generated patterns against current package documentation and local security requirements.
Request tests and operational verification for authentication, transactions, caching, and shutdown paths.
anti_patterns: Do not apply every pattern when a simpler service structure meets the requirements.
Do not copy examples without validating inputs, secrets, origins, SQL identifiers, and network exposure.
Do not treat TypeScript types as runtime validation for untrusted requests.

faq.question: Does this skill generate a complete backend application?
faq.answer: No. It provides architecture guidance and implementation patterns that must be adapted, integrated, and tested.

faq.question: Which Node.js frameworks does it cover?
faq.answer: It includes direct examples for Express and Fastify, with patterns that can inform other Node.js frameworks.

faq.question: Does it support SQL and NoSQL databases?
faq.answer: Yes. The playbook covers PostgreSQL pooling and transactions, MongoDB with Mongoose, and Redis caching.

faq.question: Can it help with authentication?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers password hashing, JWT verification, access and refresh tokens, role authorization, and authentication rate limits.

faq.question: Is the guidance ready for direct production use?
faq.answer: No. Review package versions, runtime validation, CORS, secret handling, SQL construction, caching, and deployment controls first.

faq.question: Does it include testing patterns?
faq.answer: Only a short testing recommendation is included. Detailed unit, integration, and end-to-end testing guidance is outside this skill.
